transcript: AI is changing the way we use our PCs, but have AI PCs actually become mainstream yet? Well, 87% of businesses globally are either already upgrading to AI PCs or planning to do so in their next PC refresh cycle. A standard PC has a central processing unit called CPU and a graphics processing unit called GPU. AI PCs, on the other hand, add specialized hardware called as neural processing unit, or NPU. This makes them run faster and more efficiently. With Intel Core Series 2 processors, that comes down to power, performance, and intelligence. The best of three worlds in one device. First, there's power, because all that AI capability is only useful if the laptop has enough power to support it. Core Series 2 features a power-efficient architecture with LP E-cores designed to deliver longer battery life for mobile productivity without constant charging. Zoom, Microsoft 365, and Google Workspace, the apps you use the most, are optimized for Intel Core Series 2 processors, so you can hit the ground running right out of the box. And then there is the intelligence. So, with the hardware sorted for AI, let's see how we can actually use it. One example I tried out was AI Playground Essentials, an AI app suite designed specifically for Intel Core Series 2 systems. You can use it to chat with a wide selection of AI models, choosing the one that best fits what you need, including models like Gemma, DeepSeek, and GPT. Intel also has AI PC bundles tailored to how you use your PC. So, no matter what you're using it for, the experience feels made for you, because it was.
